findings.where: Phone first screen: the order of Mark's line, the yellow 'Write to me directly' address strip and the supporting paragraph ('I advise multilateral development banks…')
findings.fault: On a phone, the address strip comes between Mark's line and the paragraph that explains it. That paragraph is the only place the first screen says who he advises and on what. On desktop it sits above the action, with the line. On a phone the visitor is asked to write to him before learning what he does, and the paragraph is left below the strip, cut off from the heading it explains.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer opening the link on a phone. They read a broad line about PPPs, then meet an email address with nothing yet to tell them this is an advisor to banks and governments. The 'why write' comes after the 'write'. The founder also judges this first screen first, and the phone tells a different story from the desktop.

findings.where: Phone first screen: the portrait against the left edge of the logo, name, nav, heading and address strip text
findings.fault: The portrait is inset about 6 px further than everything else inside the hairline frame. The text all shares one left edge and the photo does not. That breaks the clean document edge the direction is built on, and the caption is centred under the photo while all other text is left-aligned.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who is judging how refined the 'counsel's paper' sheet is. On a page whose one borrowed detail is a precise document edge, a near-miss alignment reads as careless rather than meant.

findings.where: Motion section on desktop: the easing-curve box under 'Settled, unhurried, once.'; the replayed line beside it
findings.fault: The curve box sits a few pixels in from the 426 px column that the heading above and the caption below share. Its top also doesn't line up with the top of the replayed line beside it. The section's two columns look set by eye rather than on the tile's grid.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the tile's specimen parts. Elsewhere below the fold, the label column and the content column hold their edges exactly, so this one part looks unfinished.

findings.where: Motion section on phone: the four-column timing table (Element, Start, Length, Easing)
findings.fault: On a phone the table keeps all four columns. The Element column is squeezed to about 90 px, so 'Mark's line settles: opacity 0 to 1 as it rises…' breaks into eight short lines and 'cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0, 1)' splits mid-value. The section becomes a dense, ragged block, which goes against the 'settled, unhurried' quiet it describes.
findings.who_objects: The founder or a reviewer checking the tile on a phone. The motion spec is hard to read and is the busiest part of an otherwise quiet sheet.
